argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: High: premises are stated and progressively refined across sections

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High: objections are anticipated and addressed, though not fully resolved
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High: all sections bear directly on the compatibility question
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate: key premises about nous and essence are plausible but under-theorized

explicit_definitions_given: nous as intellectual apprehension of first principles
induction as ambiguous between enumeration and recognition

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Relocates the problem from induction to nous; accepts fallibility in discovery while preserving ideal necessity
objections_raised: No finite experience can establish completeness
Essential vs accidental cannot be read off perception
Nous may be under-theorized and unreliable
Immanent universals in matter yield only for-the-most-part regularities

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, thought experiments, examples from geometry and astronomy, contrast with Platonism

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Aristotelian realism about immanent universals and essentialist natural science
philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Neutral-critical: defends Aristotle's coherence conditionally while noting unresolved epistemic gaps
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Epistemology of scientific knowledge, metaphysics of universals, induction and necessity

structural_organization.structure_type: Problem-solution-refinement with cumulative sections and conclusion

summary_of_core_decisions: The compatibility of induction and demonstrative science is secured only by interpreting induction as experience-guided intellectual recognition of immanent forms, not as enumerative inference; necessity derives from nous and causal definition, but the reliability and completeness of nous remain unresolved.
